kill_fact: No kill. Every load-bearing number in the bear case verifies against primary sources. The Q4-2026 cash cliff is exact: on the 30 July 2026 call the CFO stated Q2 operating cash flow of -$31m and net capital expenditure of $119m (3.5% of revenue), a $12m quarter-end cash balance, ~$1.7bn of liquidity, no buyback, a Q3 free-cash-flow guide of ~$100m and a reiterated full-year $500-600m guide resting on 'meaningful positive cash impacts from contract advances and incentives as well as favorable cash tax impacts in the fourth quarter'. With Q1 at -$390m operating / $74m capex, first-half free cash flow is -$614m, so Q4 must produce $1.01-1.11bn against the $516m actually delivered in Q4 2025 ($650m operating less $134m capex). The estimate-at-completion precedent is also exact: 30 Oct 2024 close $250.49 to 31 Oct 2024 close $184.96 (-26.2%, volume 2.61m against a ~320k norm) and 5 Feb 2025 $195.58 to 6 Feb 2025 $159.75 (-18.3%, volume 2.39m), trough $160.82 on 13 Feb 2025. Balance sheet at 30 June 2026 confirms net debt $2,923m including $233m of finance leases ($2,690m excluding). The single strongest attack available - that the bear inflates the opacity of the Q2 margin - is a framing correction, not a kill.
corrections:
1) THESIS-LAYER OVERSTATEMENT (the strongest finding). The bear asserts that because management twice refused to size the submarine-contract adjustment, 'investors cannot separate how much of the 6.6% segment margin was operational improvement and how much was a one-time credit'. The same call disclosed exactly that: net cumulative catch-up adjustments of +$8m at Newport News, -$2m at Ingalls and +$4m at Mission Technologies, i.e. net +$10m against segment operating income of $224m and a $52m year-on-year increase. Management declined to size only the submarine-specific slice, not the total. At most ~20% of the year-on-year margin improvement, and ~4% of segment profit, is net catch-up; the rest is volume and mix. The estimate-at-completion mechanism remains real and unretired - the two single-session collapses are verified above - but this particular inference is not supported by the disclosure.
2) The bear's 'negative 13% net estimate adjustment' at Newport News in Q3 2025 could not be verified against any primary disclosure; HII reports net cumulative catch-up adjustments in dollars, not as a percentage. Treat as unsupported. Not load-bearing - the bear's case does not rest on it.
3) 52-WEEK LOW IS WRONG BUT INERT. The record uses $259; the actual 52-week low is $262.66 (quote, 11 Aug 2026). So the shares sit 23.4% above the low, not 25%, and the twelve-month drawdown from the $460 high is -42.9%, not 44%. The sop_bear $180 is built bottom-up from segment EBITDA and net debt, not from the drawdown, so no valuation level moves - the drawdown line is only a calibration cross-check. No corrections_typed entry.
4) LANE-FIT, not valuation. The record assigns HII to the nuclear_smr chain. HII has no commercial small-modular-reactor product, no NRC reactor-design position, and does not build the naval reactors themselves (that is BWXT, one layer down). Its verified position is platform integration of government-owned naval nuclear propulsion. This is not a broad-theme substitution - the demand is name-specific and contracted - but the SMR chain tag overstates the technology adjacency and should not be read as commercial-SMR exposure.
